Messages.Body:
hi there !
okay i'm leaving my personal crusade against table split for the moment.
Just a question to ask...
if LSJ or James Coupe (yes, he became the second authority for me ;] ) can
answer, i'll be violently happy !

This case occured when the meth controlling Anson had no wakes and was low
on pool...

Joaquina plays Sensory dep on Anson. Anson Blocks. Joaquina adds 1 stealth.
Ansons follows with +1 intercept. Joaquina meth's said okay, you blocked me.
Then starts to think for a while but plays no cards. Ansons' meth says
"since i blocked you, combat will start, heh ?" Joaquina's meth doesn't
reply. Then ansons says : "i play inf. obedience, and we both stay
untapped". At this point, Joaquina's meth says "*you* stay tapped because i
play red herring now : i take back my action card". The players at the table
couldn't agree on this being legal.
Of course i was on the contesting side ;) my argument was : Red herring is
supposed to be played by acting vampire. If it hasn't been played, then
reacting vamp should play his card : obedience can be played and cancels the
combat and the block is resolved, so at this point you cannot play red
herring anymore. (I base my thoughts on how Change of target work, but it
sounds stupide to play change of target after obedience so chances are
nobody ever did)

so is red herring played Immediatly after the block is successful, or can it
be played at any time, even after obedience ?

reyda

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Reyda wrote:
> This case occured when the meth controlling Anson had no wakes and was low
> on pool...
>
> Joaquina plays Sensory dep on Anson. Anson Blocks. Joaquina adds 1 stealth.
> Ansons follows with +1 intercept. Joaquina meth's said okay, you blocked me.
> Then starts to think for a while but plays no cards. Ansons' meth says
> "since i blocked you, combat will start, heh ?" Joaquina's meth doesn't
> reply. Then ansons says : "i play inf. obedience, and we both stay
> untapped". At this point, Joaquina's meth says "*you* stay tapped because i
> play red herring now : i take back my action card". The players at the table
> couldn't agree on this being legal.

Depends on the situation. If Joaquina's meth was trying to stall in order to see
if Anson would play Obedience, this is unsportsmanlike. If she was just
using silence to acknowledge that she wished to play no effects, then she
cannot change her mind after seeing the obedience. If she was thinking about
her answer when Anson's controller jumped the gun, then she is free to do
as she did.

It's good to get into the habit of declaring (and waiting for the declaration)
of each event or pass.

A: Joaquina attempts to Sensory Dep. Anson
B: Anson blocks
A: +1 stealth
B: +1 intercept
A: I'm blocked, we're going to combat (indicating no modifiers)
B: Obedience

or

A: I'm blocked. I play Red Herring.

If, in this case, A says:

A: I'm blocked.

B should just respond "yes, you're blocked" and wait for A to proceed.

> Of course i was on the contesting side ;) my argument was : Red herring is
> supposed to be played by acting vampire. If it hasn't been played, then
> reacting vamp should play his card : obedience can be played and cancels the
> combat and the block is resolved, so at this point you cannot play red
> herring anymore. (I base my thoughts on how Change of target work, but it
> sounds stupide to play change of target after obedience so chances are
> nobody ever did)

True, but Anson can't rush the acting player or skip the acting player's
phase in order to play Obedience before Red Herring.

> so is red herring played Immediatly after the block is successful, or can it
> be played at any time, even after obedience ?

No.

--
LSJ (vte...@white-wolf.com) V:TES Net.Rep for White Wolf, Inc.

How much is mandatory to announce? An example came up this weekend,
when getting some practice in for GenCon.

The names and faces have been changed to protect all those involved:

John: "Well, looks like all your vampires are tapped! I'm attempting
a computer hacking on you with Lucretia, Cess Queen"

Rick: "Haha, too bad I will play forced awakening on smudge the
ignored with my sniper rifle!"

John: "okay, you may attempt to block."

Rick: "Any stealth?"

John: "+1, from her inate power"

Rick: "what? you didn't tell me she has stealth on every action, how
can I remember that she is one of only 3 vampires that always have +1
stealth! You should have declared that you are bleeding me with
computer hacking at stealth!"

John: "Why didn't you ask? I wasn't hiding anything from you."

Rick: "Well, I'm playing the wake on Lambach instead, because he has
the sports bike"

John: "sorry, card laid is a card played!"

Anyway, point is how much of your action need to be stated? Do you
have to read the entire text on every card you play, or is just the
name sufficient until someone asks?

I'm going to jump in here since *I am* the Rick of this Aaron's inane little
post. Aaron obviously plays the part of John if that wasn't made clear from
the biased telling of the strory...

My beef is that it should be at the very least polite and probably good
sportsmanship for the acting player to make clear all conditions regarding
an action. If I take an action that is at +1 stealth, I should *declare
explicitly* that there is +1 stealth, unless it is immediately obvious. If
it is *not* immediately obvious (such as in this particular case) then
common courtesy would dictate that the acting player do their best to make
sure their opponent knows what is happening.

So, when Aaron declares a bleed with a minion, in this case Muaziz, I
believe that he should also declare that the bleed is at +1 stealth. He
should not rely on Wes to read the 'Muaziz gets +1 stealth on all her
actions' at the bottom of the card, *regardless* of how Wes really should
know Muaziz has that ability. Cards upside down look different, blah, blah,
blah... it's just common courtesy and good sportsmanship to make sure your
opponent knows what is happening and obfuscating (no pun intended) the terms
smacks of the kind of play I don't particularly like seeing.

So, what Aaron did was technically legal--I won't bother to argue that
point. It was also cheezy and deceptive IMHO.

In my experience, were I in his position I would have made sure that he knew
the action was at +1 stealth and declared my action thus 'Muaziz will bleed
at +1 stealth' rather than just tapping a minion and saying 'Bleeds.'

Actions such as equipping or hiring a retainer etc should most of the time
be obvious as far as stealth if one has read the rules, but may need to be
declared if the opposing player is not sure. Specific cards or special
effects of vampires are *not* always obvious, so should be declared.

A player new to the game should not have to compete with the encyclopaedic
knowledge of a veteran player and it is extremely cheezy for a veteran to
take advantage of another player's inexperience with certain cards. They
should explain the cards clearly to the other player, *regardless* of
whether it benefits them to do so or not.

With all due respect to LSJ, this is not a 'rules' question... it is a
question of playing-style, courtesy and sportsmanship. It may however
interest others to see how two individuals differ on opinions on this kind
of thing. *shrug*

Cheers,
WES

Muazziz has an inherent stealth to all of her actions. But I also feel
that aaron should have said something about it for the reason stated
above.

The way I usually put this is:

I bleed with Muazziz. Do you block? If so you will need one intercept
due to her ability.

Having said that this is what I would do in a friendly weekly game.
Now in any competative event the move Aaron made is IMO simply
beautifull. He not only made you play a FA and made Smudge burn a
blood, he also got through a bleed for 2. BUT this is only in a

expires and I need the bleed for 2 to oust and take the tourney.

It is indeed a question of playing-style, courtesy and sportsmanship.
But also one of how one views the game and his/her behaviour therein.

Tim

Messages.Author: Pat Ricochet
Messages.Body:


Well, it's fine among friends, and good practice among new players.
Most everybody gives some slack at the start. However, if you're going to
play in a tournament, you won't (and shouldn't) get ANY slack. So it
behooves a playgroup to get into the habit of allowing less and less
takebacks as the players get more and more experienced, so you have a habit
of doing everything in it's time (getting pool from the Edge, blood from
hunting grounds, playing Master cards, etc.), so it doesn't cost you a game
in a tournament because you've learned an "undisciplined" playstyle.

It's also good for avoiding problems later on; "where do you draw the
line" issues come up. Good example: How long after the fact can a guy gain
blood for the Edge?
Before he plays his first Master?
Before he taps his first minion?
Before he discards?
Before the next guys turn?
(the answer, of course, is (e), none of the above; if you take blood off of
a Blood Doll or any other Master phase events, you've begun your Master
phase, and can't get pool for keeping the Edge.)
Early in a game, it's no big deal, but what if near the end of the game,
down to two of you, the other guy says "Hey, I forgot to get pool for the
Edge the last 2 turns," and plops two counters into his pool right then.
And, you *could* have ousted him that turn, until he did that; what's more,
you could still have gotten him if he had only taken 1 pool. Heated
discussion arises, and with no rule and no judge, you piss off both players,
and "well, you took pool for the Edge last game!" issues come up, etc.
Worse yet if you're playing a Prince Vote deck, and maybe have some
Parity Shifts, so he may well NOT want to take pool from the Edge, as it's
optional.

Sure, there are less extreme cases, but it all comes back to "where you
draw the line." Different strokes for different folks, and that line
usually gets drawn where everyone can agree, and sometimes you lose players
over that, since "hey! It's all fun, what's with all the rules!" players
and the "It is a *strategic* card game, if you don't follow the rules, why
are you playing?" players can both get unhappy, depending where the line is
drawn.

--
Pat Ricochet
Soul Jar'rn Fool of Atlanta

In our playgroup, in social games, we allow one "take back" type thing
per game per player, which we called a person's one "stuff up"
(although most of the time the word "stuff" got replaced with
something not allowed by VEKN sportsmanship guidlines O:). However,
after a while it became a bit difficult to draw the line between a
"stuff up" and just poor play.
Eventually we decided that where we drew the line was "information
gained". If you gained info since the time of the stuff up, you
couldn't take it back.
For example, you play a skill card in your masterphase, and don't
replace it, and realise you'd missed gaining a pool for the edge. No
information has been gained since the time when you were supposed to
gain from the edge, so you could take that as your "one stuff up". But
if you'd replaced the skill card, then you'd have gained information
(being: what the next card in your library is) so you'd not be allowed
to take it back.
Also, declaring block attempts, other people playing cards, declines
to block, etc, all count as "information gained".

For newbies just learning, though, we were a lot more lenient. Not
that that has been an issue lately as we don't really have any new
players (they say they'll turn up and learn to play, but then they
don't! the lying bastards!)

> "stuff up" and just poor play.
> Eventually we decided that where we drew the line was "information
> gained". If you gained info since the time of the stuff up, you
> couldn't take it back.

Seems a fairly good system. Maybe make them pay a pool, too? =) (kind
of makes "I forgot to get Pool for the Edge" pointless, but this way you can
blame the rule, and divert their anger. =)

[snip]

> oh, and as for proxies, we just plain don't allow that. We try and
> emphasis how it's a tradable card game. half the fun for me is
> building a deck as close as i can to my imagined "ideal", and then
> playing, see how it goes, trade to get those other cards it "needs",
> and then the deck slowly gets better, causing more and more fear each
> time it is played....play...trade..play...trade...play...get bored,
> dissassemble, start again with a new concept. O:)

Well, that works in a relatively "equal" playgroup. But when someone in
your group has more Disarms than the rest of the group put together, most of
that from just having BOUGHT that many boxes, you could, in principle, just
borrow them; but why scuff up all those cards that aren't yours? Easier to
use proxies.

> proxies are bad.

Well, I like trading as much as the next guy, and avoid using proxies as
much as I can, but:
#1 reason to use and allow proxies: Cards that you DO own, but have
more than one deck using them. I've *got* 8 Embrace (say); but I may well
have a deck with all 8, and 3 other decks that need 2-3 each. Keeping track
of all that is a royal PITA, and having to search through all your decks
just to play one of them, because you're on an "Embrace Kick," and trying
out lots of ideas/variants at once without madly shuffling cards back and
forth between games.

> it defeats the purpose of having card sets. if you allowed unlimited
> proxies, then you may as well never ever buy any cards, just print out
> the card texts from ww's site, slip them into some sleeves and away
> you go. where's the fun in that?

Well, if no one else in the group cares, it's all the fun of the regular
game. You can put 30 Disarms in your deck with your printer, fine. Your
deck will curl up and die from poor design.
But, if you want to play in tournaments, or play with groups that
*don't* allow proxies, you're SOL. And, again, you miss out on all the
trading.
It's also quite possibly illegal, especially if you do it for someone
else. 8)

Our group keeps a jar in the middle of the table. If you screw up the
order of your turn somehow (discarding before influencing, say) or
draw too many cards (darn those Bum Rushes!) or commit some other
little mistake, you have to drop a quarter into the jar. We use the
money (about $3 a night) for refreshments. It is a good compromise
between being friendly and being hard-assed.
